note: SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURES. Not real measurements. The reply classification rules below are PROVISIONAL harness rules. The authoritative wire protocol and reply-handling rules belong to the Phase 4B protocol specification and must replace them.
semantics_ref: PHASE_4_CROSS_CUTTING_TECHNICAL_DECISION_CONTRACT.md D4-6 (fields answeredInWindow, lateAnswers, duplicateAnswers, outOfOrderAnswers; unanswered = probesSent - answeredInWindow; zero answers in window is a failure, never a 100 percent figure).

rules.R-U1: Probe seq s is sent at s * interval_ms after train start.
rules.R-U2: The first reply for a seq decides it: arrival - send <= window_ms means answered in window, otherwise late.
rules.R-U3: Every later reply for an already decided seq is a duplicate, whatever its timing.
rules.R-U4: An answered-in-window reply is out of order when its seq is lower than the highest seq among earlier-arrived answered-in-window replies.
rules.R-U5: A reply whose seq is outside 0..probes_sent-1 is ignored and counted only as ignored.
rules.R-U6: unanswered = probes_sent - answered_in_window. Late replies are reported separately and are not treated as lost.
rules.R-U7: answered_in_window = 0 yields FAILED_NO_RESPONSE, never a Succeeded result.

fixtures.description: Clean train: 8 probes, every reply in order and in window.
Reordered: seq 1 (sent at 100) arrives after seq 2 (sent at 200).
Late reply: seq 5 (sent at 500) is answered at 2000, a delay of 1500 ms against a 1000 ms window. It is late, not lost, and not in window.
No replies at all. Never expressed as 100 percent loss.
Unknown sequence: a reply carries seq 99, which was never sent. It is ignored and does not touch any counter.
All replies late. By the contract's literal rule (R-U7) this is a failure with zero answered in window. Whether an all-late train deserves its own outcome is an open question in the harness document.
